extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, patent attorneys/agents submitting a terminal disclaimer to the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Filing a USPTO terminal disclaimer (PTO/SB/26) to obviate a double patenting rejection by disclaiming the terminal part of the patent term and meeting procedural/signature/payment/privacy requirements. Includes required statements, exceptions, and submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer statement (core disclaimer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner hereby disclaims, except as provided below, the terminal part of the statutory term of any patent granted on the instant application which would extend beyond the expiration date of the full statutory term of prior patent No. ________ as the term of said prior patent is presently shortened by any terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the principal operative language of the form — the owner must expressly disclaim the terminal portion of the patent term that would extend beyond the (shortened) expiration date of the identified prior patent. The form provides a blank to identify the prior patent number and the owner's percentage interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability limited to common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner hereby agrees that any patent so granted on the instant application shall be enforceable only for and during such period that it and the prior patent are commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclaimer must include an agreement that enforceability of the granted patent is limited to the period of common ownership with the prior patent; the agreement runs with any patent granted on the instant application and binds grantee, successors, and assigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the disclaimer runs with the patent and binds successors
rubrics_metrics.description: This agreement runs with any patent granted on the instant application and is binding upon the grantee, its successors or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form language makes clear the disclaimer is attached to the patent itself and creates obligations on future owners; include this language when completing the disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions where owner does not disclaim (situations preserving later extended term)
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the above disclaimer, the owner does not disclaim the terminal part of the term of any patent granted on the instant application that would extend to the expiration date of the full statutory term of the prior patent ... in the event that said prior patent later: (a) expires for failure to pay a maintenance fee; (b) is held unenforceable; (c) is found invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction; (d) is statutorily disclaimed in whole or terminally disclaimed under 37 CFR 1.321; (e) has all claims canceled by a reexamination certificate; (f) is reissued; or (g) is in any manner terminated prior to the expiration of its full statutory term as presently shortened by any terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of concrete events that, if they occur to the prior patent, permit the owner NOT to have disclaimed the terminal portion that would correspond to the prior patent's full statutory term. The form requires these exceptions to be explicitly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for organizations (box 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions on behalf of a business/organization ..., the undersigned is empowered to act on behalf of the business/organization. I hereby declare that all statements made herein of my own knowledge are true ... made with the knowledge that willful false statements ... are punishable by fine or imprisonment ... under Section 1001 of Title 18 of the United States Code and that such willful false statements may jeopardize the validity of the application or any patent issued thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing on behalf of an organization, the signer must have authority and must make the statutory declaration of truthfulness; the form contains the required attestation language and warns of criminal penalties for false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory as attorney or agent of record (box 2) and required registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: The undersigned is an attorney or agent of record. Reg. No. ________ [signature block, typed/printed name, date, telephone number].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclaimer is signed by an attorney/agent of record, include the registration number and the standard signature block information (signature, date, typed name, phone). The form provides the layout for these entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer fee under 37 CFR 1.20(d) must be included
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminal disclaimer fee under 37 CFR 1.20(d) included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form requires payment of the applicable terminal disclaimer fee as specified in 37 CFR 1.20(d). The filer should ensure payment is submitted per USPTO payment procedures (see PTO-2038 or other accepted payment channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning: do not include credit card information on the form
rubrics_metrics.description: WARNING: Information on this form may become public. Credit card information should not be included on this form. Provide credit card information and authorization on PTO-2038.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because information on the submitted form may be disclosed publicly, do not place credit card numbers or authorization on PTO/SB/26; use PTO-2038 or other secure payment mechanisms for payment details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 3.73(b) certification required if signed by assignee (owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: *Statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b) is required if terminal disclaimer is signed by the assignee (owner). Form PTO/SB/96 may be used for making this certification. See MPEP § 324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignee (owner) signs the terminal disclaimer, an additional statement/certification under 37 CFR 3.73(b) is required; the form references PTO/SB/96 as a tool and cites MPEP §324 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission instructions and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need assistance in completing the form, call 1-800-PTO-9199 and select option 2. If filing this completed form by mail, send to: Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. DO NOT SEND FEES OR COMPLETED FORMS TO [Privacy Act address].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form includes phone contact for assistance and specific mailing instructions. It explicitly warns not to send fees or completed forms to the Privacy Act address printed on the form; follow the mailing/payment instructions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act Statement and consequence of non-furnishing information
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO collects the information under authority of 35 U.S.C. 2 ... If you do not furnish the information requested on this form, the USPTO may not be able to process and/or examine your submission, which may result in termination of proceedings, abandonment of the application, and/or expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Privacy Act statement explains the statutory basis for collection, routine uses (law enforcement, other agencies, contractors, courts, GSA, national security review, OPM, OMB), and the practical consequences of failing to provide the requested information (possible termination/abandonment/expiration).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB control number and estimated public burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved for use through 11/30/2027. OMB 0651-0031 ... Public burden for this form is estimated to average 15 minutes per response, including time for reviewing instructions, searching existing data sources, gathering and maintaining the data needed, and completing and reviewing the information collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form displays the OMB control number and an estimated time burden; filers may provide comments regarding the burden estimate to the Chief Administrative Officer at the USPTO.
